 Prayer : Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of Cons
 India, to issue Writ of Mandamus directing the respondents 1 and 2 to fr
 Rules by providing promotional avenues for the members of the petitioner
 Association who are working as Food Inspectors by providing first prefer
 to them who are qualified and eligible for promotion as per 2.1.2:1 (iii
 the Fssa Rules as Designated Officers in the Department of Food, Safety 
 Drug Administration, Government of Tamil Nadu by taking into considerati
 the representation made by the petitioner's Association dated 18.01.2016
 For Petitioner : Mr.K.Srinivasamurthy
 For Respondents : Mr.P.Kumaresan  Additional Advocate Gen  Assisted by  Mr.K.Tippu Sulthan  Government Advocate for  No appearance for R3  ORDER This writ petition has been filed for issuance of a Writ of Mandamus directing the respondents 1 and 2 to frame rules by providing promotional avenues for the members of the petitioner Association who are working as Food Inspectors by providing first preference to them who are qualified and eligible https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis for promotion as per 2.1.2:1 (iii) (a) of the FSSA Rules as Designated Officers in the Department of Food, Safety and Drug Administration, Government of Tamil Nadu by taking into consideration the representation made by the petitioner's Association dated 18.01.2016.
2. The members of the petitioner Association are all B.Sc., Chemistry graduates and joined the Municipal Administration Department of the Government of Tamil Nadu as Sanitary Inspectors/
Sanitary Officers in the local bodies viz., the Corporations and Municipalities. The petitioners were sent for training in terms of Section 9 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 r/w Rule 8 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1955 and on completion of training posted as Food Inspectors. After the Food, Safety and Standards Act, 2008 came into force on 05.08.2011, the petitioners were appointed as Food Safety Officers in the 2nd respondent Department and are continuing as such. The petitioners claim promotion to the post of designated officers but the respondents have not framed any rules for promotion of the Inspectors to the post of designated officers. The petitioners therefore filed the writ petition. 
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Rep. By Its State General Secretary vs The Government Of Tamil Nadu on 30 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142326436/
2 3. At the time of hearing, the learned Additional Advocate General submitted that the Government is in process of framing rules for the designated officers and a committee is also formed for the purpose. The learned Additional Advocate General, therefore seeks short time for finalising the rules and for publishing the same. 
4. In view of the fact that the Government is in the process of framing rules for the designated officers, the writ petition is disposed of with a direction to the respondents to complete the process of framing the service rules and notifying the rules for the post of designated officers within a period of four months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order. 
5. With the above direction and observation, this writ petition is disposed of. No costs. 
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is also closed.
